github:github/gh-aw#51412.title: Audit helper-built thrown Error messages
github:github/gh-aw#51412.body:
`require-error-code-in-thrown-error` skipped `throw new Error(helper())`, so helper-built messages in coded files could bypass error-code checks entirely. This left uncoded validation messages accepted silently beside coded sibling errors.

- **ESLint rule**
  - Audits simple same-file helper calls with a single static return.
  - Adds `callExpressionNeedsReview` for imported, branched, dynamic, or indirect helper-call messages that cannot be verified statically.
  - Preserves existing low-confidence silence for unrelated non-message expressions.

```js
throw new Error(helper()); // audited if helper is local/static; otherwise flagged for review
```

- **MCP validation messages**
  - Prefixes `generateEnhancedErrorMessage()` return paths with `ERR_VALIDATION`.
  - Keeps enhanced schema guidance unchanged after the code prefix.

- **Tests**
  - Covers coded local helpers, uncoded local helpers, dynamic helpers, imported helpers, indirect helper-call messages, and branched helpers.
  - Updates enhanced-error expectations for the new validation code prefix.

github:github/gh-aw#44650.title: Consolidate `copilot-requests: write` permission checks on `Permissions`
github:github/gh-aw#44650.body:
The `copilot-requests: write` gate was implemented three times across workflow and CLI paths, with each call site re-deriving the same `Permissions` lookup. This change moves the check onto `*Permissions` so all callers share one source of truth for Copilot token-auth enablement.

- **Shared permission helper**
  - Add `(*Permissions).HasCopilotRequestsWrite()` to centralize the `copilot-requests: write` check, including safe nil handling.

- **Call site consolidation**
  - Route workflow execution permission checks through the shared helper.
  - Route compiler tip emission logic through the shared helper while preserving the existing explicit `none` override behavior.
  - Route CLI workflow secret detection through the shared helper after frontmatter parsing.

- **Coverage**
  - Add focused permission tests for shorthand, explicit, nil, and override cases.
  - Add validator-level coverage to verify the Copilot enablement tip still emits only when the write permission is not effectively granted.

```go
func (p *Permissions) HasCopilotRequestsWrite() bool {
	if p == nil {
		return false
	}
	level, ok := p.Get(PermissionCopilotRequests)
	return ok && level == PermissionWrite
}
```

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,48 @@
+# ADR-44650: Consolidate `copilot-requests: write` Permission Check on `*Permissions`
+
+**Date**: 2026-07-10
+**Status**: Draft
+**Deciders**: pelikhan (PR author), copilot-swe-agent (implementor)
+
+---
+
+### Context
+
+The `copilot-requests: write` permission check — determining whether a workflow has granted Copilot token-auth enablement — was implemented inline at three separate call sites: `hasCopilotRequestsWritePermission` in `pkg/workflow/permissions_operations.go`, `shouldEmitCopilotRequestsEnableTip` in `pkg/workflow/permissions_compiler_validator.go`, and `hasCopilotRequestsWritePermission` in `pkg/cli/workflow_secrets.go`. Each re-derived the same `perms.Get(PermissionCopilotRequests) && level == PermissionWrite` logic independently. The `*Permissions` type already hosted an analogous method, `HasContentsReadAccess()`, establishing a prior pattern for centralising permission predicates on the type.
+
+### Decision
+
+We will add `(*Permissions).HasCopilotRequestsWrite() bool` as the single source of truth for the `copilot-requests: write` check. All three existing call sites are updated to delegate to this method. The method handles nil receivers, consistent with the existing `HasContentsReadAccess()` pattern.
+
+### Alternatives Considered
+
+#### Alternative 1: Keep Inline Checks at Each Call Site (Status Quo)
+
+Each call site continues to call `perms.Get(PermissionCopilotRequests)` and compare the result to `PermissionWrite`. No shared helper is introduced.
+
+This was rejected because the three implementations can silently diverge over time (e.g., one site adds nil-guard logic that the others miss), making the effective permission rule difficult to reason about and audit.
+
+#### Alternative 2: Extract a Package-Level Helper Function
+
+A package-private function `hasCopilotRequestsWrite(p *Permissions) bool` is extracted rather than adding a method to `*Permissions`.
+
+This was rejected because a method on `*Permissions` is consistent with the existing `HasContentsReadAccess()` pattern, keeps the nil-safety concern inside the type, and is discoverable by callers who already hold a `*Permissions` value.
+
+### Consequences
+
+#### Positive
+- Single location for the `copilot-requests: write` business rule — future changes to how this permission is evaluated affect all call sites uniformly.
+- Built-in nil safety — callers no longer need to guard against a nil `*Permissions` before checking the permission.
+- Follows the established `Has*` method convention on `*Permissions`, improving API consistency.
+
+#### Negative
+- Increases the public API surface of the `Permissions` type by one exported method.
+- A bug introduced in `HasCopilotRequestsWrite()` now propagates to all three callers simultaneously, whereas previously each call site could only affect its own code path.
+
+#### Neutral
+- No change in observable behaviour at the call sites — the refactor is behaviour-preserving by construction.
+- New unit tests are added for `HasCopilotRequestsWrite()` directly, covering nil, shorthand write-all, read-all, explicit write, explicit none, and write-all-with-explicit-none override cases.
+
+---
+
+*ADR created by [adr-writer agent]. Review and finalize before changing status from Draft to Accepted.*

github:github/gh-aw#43083.title: Quick Start: define frontmatter inline and surface `.lock.yml` semantics as a callout
github:github/gh-aw#43083.body:
Quick Start used “frontmatter” without enough in-context definition for first-time users, and the `.lock.yml` explanation was easy to miss in plain body text. This update keeps content intact while improving scanability and beginner comprehension through presentation-only edits.

- **Step 4 terminology clarity**
  - Updated first use of `frontmatter` to include an inline definition: “the **YAML configuration block** between the `---` markers...”.

- **`.lock.yml` explanation visibility**
  - Wrapped the existing `.lock.yml` explanation in a `[!NOTE]` callout so it stands out during skimming.

- **Scope**
  - Single-file docs change in `docs/src/content/docs/setup/quick-start.mdx`.
  - No removal of existing guidance; only wording/presentation adjustments.

```mdx
> [!NOTE]
> The `.lock.yml` is the compiled GitHub Actions workflow generated from your markdown — it is what actually runs, and it is regenerated automatically, so you never edit it by hand.
```

github:github/gh-aw#54376.body: The `CGO` workflow job failed on `main` because the `golint-custom` `errormessage` analyzer flagged 24 error messages introduced by the Agent Plugins support change (`exit code 3`) for non-actionable wording. ## Root cause The custom linter rejects two patterns: - generic `fmt.Errorf("failed to ...: %w", err)` wrapping with no recovery guidance - messages containing negative language (`must`/`cannot`/`invalid`/`failed`) without constructive guidance (`expected`/`requires`/`should`/`example`) ## Changes - **Reworded flagged messages** across `pkg/parser/import_field_extractor.go`, `pkg/workflow/agentic_engine.go`, `pkg/workflow/behavior_defined_engine.go`, `pkg/workflow/compiler_yaml_ai_execution.go`, `pkg/workflow/compiler_yaml_header.go`, `pkg/workflow/plugins_frontmatter.go`, `pkg/workflow/plugins_ref_resolution.go`, `pkg/workflow/safe_update_manifest.go`, and `pkg/workflow/workflow_builder.go` to state what's expected instead of just what failed, matching the existing convention elsewhere in the codebase (`invalid X, expected Y: %w`). - **Updated 4 unit tests** in `pkg/workflow/compiler_orchestrator_workflow_test.go` that asserted the old exact error-message substrings. No behavioral changes — only error message text. ```go // before return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to resolve agentic engine from AI configuration: %w", err) // after return nil, fmt.Errorf("agentic engine could not be resolved from the 'engine' field, expected a supported engine id such as 'copilot' or 'claude': %w", err) ``` --- > Generated by [👨‍🍳 PR Sous Chef](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/actions/runs/32432532165) · gpt54 · 23.6 AIC · ⌖ 8.21 AIC · ⊞ 9.3K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Agithub%2Fgh-aw+%22gh-aw-workflow-call-id%3A+github%2Fgh-aw%2Fpr-sous-chef%22&type=pullrequests) > Comment /souschef to run again

github:github/gh-aw#42597.title: Add `tone_variant` A/B campaign to `breaking-change-checker` workflow
github:github/gh-aw#42597.body:
This updates `breaking-change-checker` to run an A/B experiment on reporting tone (`neutral` vs `urgent`) without changing breaking-change detection logic. The campaign metadata and prompt conditionals were added so tone can be assigned at runtime and compared against engagement and guardrail metrics.

- **Experiment frontmatter**
  - Added `experiments.tone_variant` in rich-object form with:
    - `variants`, `description`, `hypothesis`
    - `metric`, `secondary_metrics`
    - `guardrail_metrics` (`run_success_rate`, `empty_output_rate`)
    - `min_samples`, `weight`, `start_date`, `issue`

- **Prompt-body tone branching**
  - Added variant-aware handlebars conditionals in the issue-generation instructions:
    - tone guidance block (`urgent` vs `neutral`)
    - `Summary -> Status` line (`Requires Immediate Review` vs `Review Recommended`)
    - `Recommendations` wording (prioritized risk/action framing vs neutral guidance)

- **Compiled workflow output**
  - Regenerated `breaking-change-checker.lock.yml` from the markdown workflow so runtime experiment selection and outputs reflect the new campaign.

```md
{{#if experiments.tone_variant == "urgent" }}
- **Status**: ⚠️ Requires Immediate Review
{{else}}
- **Status**: Review Recommended
{{/if}}
```

github:github/gh-aw#54950.title: Fix engine/permission detection in lockfile-stats analyzer
github:github/gh-aw#54950.body:
The Lockfile Statistics analyzer reported empty engine and permission distributions across all 289 compiled lockfiles: its heuristics looked for a top-level `engine:` key and a top-level `permissions:` block, neither of which the compiler emits in a usable form. This updates the analyzer prompt in `.github/workflows/lockfile-stats.md` to parse where the data actually lives.

### What the compiler actually emits

```yaml
# gh-aw-metadata: {"schema_version":"v4",...,"agent_id":"claude","engine_versions":{"claude":"2.1.237"}}

permissions: {}          # always empty — carries no signal (289/289 files)

jobs:
  agent:
    permissions:         # mirrors workflow frontmatter permissions (289/289 files)
      contents: read
      issues: read
      pull-requests: read
```

### Changes

- **Engine detection**: resolve from the first-line `# gh-aw-metadata:` JSON `agent_id`, also capturing `agent_model` / `engine_versions`; fallbacks to the sole `engine_versions` key, then a `GH_AW_ENGINE_ID` env value, with an `engine_unknown` count.
- **Permission detection**: derive from per-job `jobs.<name>.permissions` rather than the always-empty top-level block — `agent_job_permissions` as the primary per-workflow scope, `permissions_by_scope` read/write/none counts, and `union_job_permissions` across all jobs; handles scalar `read-all` / `write-all` / `{}` forms and reports `permissions_unknown`.
- **Fail-loud rule**: engine and permission distributions may not be silently empty; an all-unknown result must be reported as such instead of published as zero.
- **Report format**: explicitly sources permission patterns from the agent job and engine distribution from the metadata comment.
- **Script version**: bumped `lockfile_stats_v2.py` → `lockfile_stats_v3.py` (summary schema changed) per the prompt's own versioning rule, updating every reference; `.lock.yml` regenerated.

A throwaway prototype of the documented rules run over all 289 lockfiles resolved 0 unknown engines and 0 unknown permission blocks, producing a real distribution (copilot 175, claude 60, pi 22, codex 15, …) and per-scope read/write maps.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

- Fixes #54945

 Use a single bash command that:
 
 1. Creates `/tmp/gh-aw/cache-memory/scripts` and `/tmp/gh-aw/agent`.
-2. Reuses `/tmp/gh-aw/cache-memory/scripts/lockfile_stats_v2.py` if it already exists.
+2. Reuses `/tmp/gh-aw/cache-memory/scripts/lockfile_stats_v3.py` if it already exists.
 3. Otherwise writes that script once, then executes it.
 4. Produces `/tmp/gh-aw/agent/lockfile-stats-summary.json` (compact, target ≤50KB; if larger, reduce examples before writing).
-5. If the prompt version is bumped (for example to `lockfile_stats_v3.py`), do not reuse older script versions; use the version referenced in this prompt.

github:github/gh-aw#48718.title: feat: parallelize forecast usage-artifact downloads to fix 45-min timeout
github:github/gh-aw#48718.body:
`gh aw forecast --days 30` was downloading usage artifacts for each completed workflow run serially; as run volume in `github/gh-aw` grew, the download phase alone exceeded the 45-minute job timeout with zero output produced.

## Changes

- **Parallel artifact download** (`forecast_compute.go`): replaces the serial per-run `forecastLoadCachedRunAIC` call inside `forecastWorkflow` with a new `parallelLoadRunAICs` helper that fans out downloads across a semaphore-bounded goroutine pool (default: 8 concurrent downloads), then processes results in original run order.

  ```go
  // Before: serial, one download per loop iteration
  for _, r := range completed {
      runAIC := forecastLoadCachedRunAIC(ctx, r.DatabaseID, config.Verbose)
      ...
  }

  // After: all downloads in parallel, then process in order
  aicMap := parallelLoadRunAICs(ctx, completed, config)
  for _, r := range completed {
      runAIC := aicMap[r.DatabaseID]
      ...
  }
  ```

- **`--concurrency` flag** (`forecast_command.go`): exposes `DownloadConcurrency` in `ForecastConfig` and as a CLI flag (default `0` = use the code default of 8; pass `1` for serial behaviour). The constant `defaultForecastDownloadConcurrency = 8` lives in `forecast_compute.go`.

- **Context cancellation**: `parallelLoadRunAICs` respects context cancellation at the semaphore-acquire step, so the existing `--timeout` flag cleanly interrupts in-flight downloads.

- **Tests**: covers correct result collection with concurrency, graceful early exit on cancelled context, empty-input edge case, and flag registration.

github:github/gh-aw#49685.title: fix: move Python venv out of agent artifact upload path to restore MCP telemetry observability
github:github/gh-aw#49685.body:
The `daily-performance-summary` workflow was flagged as missing MCP telemetry (`gateway.jsonl` / `rpc-messages.jsonl`) — but both files ARE generated. The root cause: shared Python setup components created a venv at `/tmp/gh-aw/agent/venv`, which is unconditionally included in the compiler-generated agent artifact upload path (`/tmp/gh-aw/agent/`). This inflated the artifact to ~253 MB / ~19,448 files (numpy, pandas, matplotlib, scipy + all deps), causing observability report downloads to time out before locating the MCP telemetry files.

## Changes

- **`shared/trending-charts-simple.md`**, **`shared/python-nlp.md`**, **`shared/python-dataviz.md`**: Changed Python venv location from `/tmp/gh-aw/agent/venv` → `/tmp/gh-aw/python/venv`

`/tmp/gh-aw/python/` is not in the artifact upload path list, so the venv is no longer uploaded. Agent artifacts for affected workflows drop from ~253 MB back to a few MB of actual log files.

```diff
- if [ ! -d /tmp/gh-aw/agent/venv ]; then
-   python3 -m venv /tmp/gh-aw/agent/venv
+ # Use /tmp/gh-aw/python/venv to avoid polluting the agent artifact upload path (/tmp/gh-aw/agent/)
+ if [ ! -d /tmp/gh-aw/python/venv ]; then
+   python3 -m venv /tmp/gh-aw/python/venv
  fi
- echo "/tmp/gh-aw/agent/venv/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
+ echo "/tmp/gh-aw/python/venv/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
```

All 268 workflows recompiled. Affects any workflow importing these shared components.

  echo "Using cached data from ${TODAY}"
  echo "Total PRs in cache: $(jq 'length' /tmp/gh-aw/agent/pr-data/copilot-prs.json)"
else
  echo "⬇ Downloading fresh PR data..."
  
  # Calculate date 30 days ago
  DATE_30_DAYS_AGO=$(date -d '30 days ago' '+%Y-%m-%d' 2>/dev/null || date -v-30d '+%Y-%m-%d')

  # Search for PRs from copilot/* branches in the last 30 days using gh CLI
  # Using branch prefix search (head:copilot/) instead of author for reliability

  gh pr list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
    --search "head:copilot/ created:>=${DATE_30_DAYS_AGO}" \
    --state all \
    --json number,title,author,headRefName,createdAt,state,url,body,labels,updatedAt,closedAt,mergedAt \
    --limit 1000 \
    > /tmp/gh-aw/agent/pr-data/copilot-prs.json

  ./.github/skills/jqschema/jqschema.sh < /tmp/gh-aw/agent/pr-data/copilot-prs.json > /tmp/gh-aw/agent/pr-data/copilot-prs-schema.json

  # Store in cache with today's date
  cp /tmp/gh-aw/agent/pr-data/copilot-prs.json "$CACHE_DIR/copilot-prs-${TODAY}.json"
  cp /tmp/gh-aw/agent/pr-data/copilot-prs-schema.json "$CACHE_DIR/copilot-prs-${TODAY}-schema.json"

  echo "✓ PR data saved to cache: copilot-prs-${TODAY}.json"
  echo "Total PRs found: $(jq 'length' /tmp/gh-aw/agent/pr-data/copilot-prs.json)"
fi

# Always ensure data is available at expected locations for backward compatibility

echo "Schema available at: /tmp/gh-aw/agent/pr-data/copilot-prs-schema.json"

github:github/gh-aw#47241.title: test: add regression guard for audit tool exposure in gh aw mcp-server
github:github/gh-aw#47241.body:
The daily CLI tools tester reported `audit` missing from `gh aw mcp-server --help` — the tool was not accessible via the MCP interface. Investigation confirmed the implementation was already correct: `registerAuditTool` is called in `createMCPServer`, `audit` appears in the command's `Long` description, and `TestMCPServerUnit_ListTools` verifies all 10 tools are registered. The issue was filed against an older binary.

## Changes

- **`pkg/cli/mcp_server_command_test.go`** — Adds `TestNewMCPServerCommand_AuditToolListedInHelp` as a regression guard ensuring `audit` is always documented in the `mcp-server` command's long description, preventing silent removal from the help text.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

- Fixes #47209

files.patch:
@@ -15,3 +15,14 @@ func TestNewMCPServerCommand_PortExampleMentionsSSE(t *testing.T) {
 
 	assert.Contains(t, cmd.Example, "Run HTTP server on port 8080 with SSE transport", "Port example should match SSE transport behavior")
 }
+
+// TestNewMCPServerCommand_AuditToolListedInHelp verifies that the audit tool
+// is documented in the mcp-server command's Long description.
+// This is a regression test for https://github.com/github/gh-aw/issues/47209
+// where audit was absent from the MCP server tool list.
+func TestNewMCPServerCommand_AuditToolListedInHelp(t *testing.T) {
+	cmd := NewMCPServerCommand()
+	require.NotNil(t, cmd)
+
+	assert.Contains(t, cmd.Long, "audit", "mcp-server long description should list the audit tool")
+}

github:github/gh-aw#56325.title: Enforce jsonschema formats and structural error path lookup
github:github/gh-aw#56325.body:
`format` constraints in gh-aw schemas were not consistently asserted during schema validation, allowing invalid `date` and `uri` values to pass in some validation paths. Composite jsonschema errors also still depended on message parsing to locate nested `additionalProperties` failures.

- **Schema compilation**
  - Enable `AssertFormat()` in the shared jsonschema compiler used by parser and workflow schema validation.
  - This makes declared formats such as `date` and `uri` validation errors instead of annotations.

```go
compiler := jsonschema.NewCompiler()
compiler.AssertFormat()
```

- **Validation error location**
  - Carry nested `ValidationError.Causes` through `JSONPathInfo`.
  - Recursively inspect composite error causes (`oneOf`, `anyOf`, `allOf`, `Group`) for `kind.AdditionalProperties`.
  - Avoid regex fallback when structured jsonschema error data is available.

- **Coverage**
  - Add focused tests for draft 2020-12 format assertion.
  - Add tests for structural `additionalProperties` discovery inside composite validation errors.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

- Fixes #56317

github:github/gh-aw#55836.title: Warn when workflow dispatches share conclusion concurrency
github:github/gh-aw#55836.body: `workflow_dispatch` fan-out silently serializes generated conclusion jobs when `concurrency.job-discriminator` is omitted, reducing throughput while runs remain green. - **Compiler warning** - Warn when a workflow includes `workflow_dispatch` without a job discriminator. - Explain that dispatches share one conclusion concurrency group. - Recommend a per-run discriminator: ```yaml concurrency: job-discriminator: ${{ github.run_id }} ``` - **Coverage** - Cover dispatch inputs, mixed triggers, configured discriminators, and non-dispatch workflows. - Fixes #55813 --- > Generated by [👨‍🍳 PR Sous Chef](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/actions/runs/32896118186) · pi · gpt54 · 11 AIC · ⌖ 8.12 AIC · ⊞ 8.7K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Agithub%2Fgh-aw+%22gh-aw-workflow-call-id%3A+github%2Fgh-aw%2Fpr-sous-chef%22&type=pullrequests) > Comment /souschef to run again --- Run: https://github.com/github/gh-aw/actions/runs/32897609333 > Generated by [👨‍🍳 PR Sous Chef](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/actions/runs/32897609333) · pi · gpt54 · 14.9 AIC · ⌖ 8.16 AIC · ⊞ 8.7K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Agithub%2Fgh-aw+%22gh-aw-workflow-call-id%3A+github%2Fgh-aw%2Fpr-sous-chef%22&type=pullrequests) > Comment /souschef to run again --- > Generated by [👨‍🍳 PR Sous Chef](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/actions/runs/32949103424) · pi · gpt54 · 20.8 AIC · ⌖ 8.13 AIC · ⊞ 8.7K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Agithub%2Fgh-aw+%22gh-aw-workflow-call-id%3A+github%2Fgh-aw%2Fpr-sous-chef%22&type=pullrequests) > Comment /souschef to run again

@@ -0,0 +1,101 @@
+//go:build !integration
+
+package workflow
+
+import (
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/github/gh-aw/pkg/testutil"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
+)
+
+func TestWorkflowDispatchConcurrencyWarning(t *testing.T) {
+	tests := []struct {
+		name          string
+		on            string
+		discriminator string
+		safeOutputs   bool
+		expectWarning bool
+	}{
+		{
+			name:          "workflow dispatch without discriminator",
+			on:            "on: workflow_dispatch",
+			safeOutputs:   true,
+			expectWarning: false,
+		},
+		{
+			name:          "workflow dispatch with empty inputs without discriminator",
+			on:            "on:\n  workflow_dispatch:\n    inputs: {}",
+			safeOutputs:   true,
+			expectWarning: false,
+		},
+		{
+			name:          "workflow dispatch with inputs without discriminator",
+			on:            "on:\n  workflow_dispatch:\n    inputs:\n      target_repo:\n        type: string",
+			safeOutputs:   true,
+			expectWarning: true,
+		},
+		{
+			name:          "workflow dispatch with inputs without safe outputs",
+			on:            "on:\n  workflow_dispatch:\n    inputs:\n      target_repo:\n        type: string",
+			expectWarning: false,
+		},
+		{
+			name:          "mixed workflow dispatch without discriminator",
+			on:            "on:\n  workflow_dispatch:\n  schedule:\n    - cron: '0 0 * * *'",
+			safeOutputs:   true,
+			expectWarning: false,
+		},
+		{
+			name:          "mixed workflow dispatch with inputs without discriminator",
+			on:            "on:\n  workflow_dispatch:\n    inputs:\n      target_repo:\n        type: string\n  schedule:\n    - cron: '0 0 * * *'",
+			safeOutputs:   true,
+			expectWarning: true,
+		},
+		{
+			name:          "workflow dispatch with inputs and discriminator",
+			on:            "on:\n  workflow_dispatch:\n    inputs:\n      target_repo:\n        type: string",
+			discriminator: "${{ github.run_id }}",
+			safeOutputs:   true,
+			expectWarning: false,
+		},
+		{
+			name:          "nested workflow dispatch value without discriminator",
+			on:            "on:\n  workflow_run:\n    workflows: [workflow_dispatch]\n    types: [completed]",
+			safeOutputs:   true,
+			expectWarning: false,
+		},
+		{
+			name:          "schedule without discriminator",
+			on:            "on:\n  schedule:\n    - cron: '0 0 * * *'",
+			safeOutputs:   true,
+			expectWarning: false,
+		},
+	}
+
+	const warning = "workflow_dispatch workflow has no concurrency.job-discriminator"
+	for _, tt := range tests {
+		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			compiler := NewCompiler()
+			workflowData := &WorkflowData{
+				On:                          tt.on,
+				ConcurrencyJobDiscriminator: tt.discriminator,
+			}
+			if tt.safeOutputs {
+				workflowData.SafeOutputs = &SafeOutputsConfig{}
+			}
+
+			output := testutil.CaptureStderr(t, func() {
+				compiler.emitGeneralToolWarnings(workflowData, "test.md")
+			})
+
+			if tt.expectWarning {
+				assert.Contains(t, output, warning)
+				assert.Equal(t, 1, compiler.GetWarningCount())
+			} else {
+				assert.NotContains(t, output, warning)
+				assert.Zero(t, compiler.GetWarningCount())
+			}
+		})
+	}
+}

github:github/gh-aw#46459.title: docs(adr): SPDD gap-fill for ADRs 26385, 26482, 26535, 26544, 26551
github:github/gh-aw#46459.body:
Five Draft ADRs (indices 25–29) had incomplete REASONS sections, missing safeguard definitions, and no path from Draft → Accepted. This addresses all eight SPDD checklist items.

### ADR-26535 — Event-Scoped Activation Permission Derivation
- **Fallback Behavior**: `SHOULD fall back … and MUST emit` → `MUST fall back … and MUST emit`; adds done condition (CI test asserts log line on empty `on:` fallback path)
- **Metadata Field Filtering**: Replaces the "e.g." hint with the complete explicit allowlist; documents that spec and `activationMetadataTriggerFields` in `compiler_activation_job.go` are verified identical

### ADR-26385 — Fast Text Pre-flight for Template Injection Validation
- Adds `### Safeguards` section: Go YAML library upgrade review trigger, new block scalar variant coverage, false-negative CI gate (one test per `|`/`>`/`|-`/`|+`/`>-`/`>+` variant), and `BenchmarkCompileComplexWorkflow` regression gate (≤ 3.0 ms/op)

### ADR-26482 — Peel Annotated Tags to Commit SHA
- Adds `### Rate-Limit Handling Norms`: MUST fail with descriptive error on rate-limit (never silently emit tag-object SHA); SHOULD NOT auto-retry within a single invocation; error MUST include tag ref + HTTP status
- Clarifies `ParseTagRefTSV` is an internal exported symbol with no SemVer implications

### ADR-26551 — Migrate GitHub App Token Input to `client-id`
- Adds `### Sync Task` scheduling the rename `GitHubAppConfig.AppID` → `GitHubAppConfig.ClientID`, struct tag updates, compile-time deprecation warning for `app-id` frontmatter, and planned removal in next major version

### ADR-26544 — BYOK-Copilot Feature Flag Composition
- Feature Composition Logic item 3: `SHOULD log` → `MUST log` for implicit `cli-proxy` activation; adds requirement for a corresponding test assertion

### All five ADRs
- Adds `### Status Promotion` checklist to each, specifying concrete Draft → Accepted criteria (merged PR, green CI, specific test requirements, no open conformance issues)

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

- Fixes #46458

 An implementation is considered conformant with this ADR if it satisfies all **MUST** and **MUST NOT** requirements above. In particular, conformance requires that the pre-flight check never returns `false` when an unsafe expression is present inside a `run:` block (no false negatives), and that the full YAML parse is skipped when the pre-flight returns `false`. Failure to meet any **MUST** or **MUST NOT** requirement constitutes non-conformance.
 
+### Safeguards
+
+The line-by-line text scanner is a custom parser that can drift from YAML semantics. The following conditions **MUST** trigger a re-evaluation of the scanner implementation before the next release:
+
+1. **Go YAML library upgrade**: Any upgrade to the `go-yaml` (or `goccy/go-yaml`) dependency version **MUST** be accompanied by a review of the scanner's block-scalar and indentation-handling logic to verify that the library's normalisation behaviour (e.g., tab-to-space conversion) remains compatible with the scanner's assumptions.
+2. **New block scalar variants**: If the YAML specification or the Go YAML library introduces support for new block scalar indicators or chomping modifiers not currently listed in normative requirement 5 of the Template Injection Pre-flight Check section, those indicators **MUST** be added to the scanner before the change is merged.
+3. **False-negative CI gate**: The CI test suite **MUST** include at least one negative test case for each `run:` block scalar variant (`|`, `>`, `|-`, `|+`, `>-`, `>+`) asserting that an unsafe expression embedded in that block content causes `hasUnsafeExpressionInRunContent` to return `true`. These tests serve as the catch-all regression gate for scanner false-negatives.
+4. **Benchmark regression gate**: The `BenchmarkCompileComplexWorkflow` benchmark **MUST NOT** regress by more than 10% relative to the established baseline, consistent with the existing CI enforcement in `cgo.yml` (benchstat >10% regression gate). An absolute performance budget of `<500ms` per compilation is the baseline target documented in `compiler_performance_benchmark_test.go`. If a change causes a >10% regression relative to the prior baseline, the scanner implementation must be profiled and optimised before the change is merged. Do not introduce a second absolute threshold (e.g., a fixed ms/op cap) that is not enforced by CI, as this creates a gap between the spec and the enforcement mechanism.
+
+---
+
+### Status Promotion
+
+This ADR is currently **Draft**. To promote it to **Accepted**, all of the following criteria must be satisfied:
+
+- [ ] The PR implementing `hasUnsafeExpressionInRunContent` has been merged to the default branch.
+- [ ] All CI checks (tests, linters, compilation) are green on the merged commit.
+- [ ] The CI test suite contains negative test cases for every `run:` block scalar variant (`|`, `>`, `|-`, `|+`, `>-`, `>+`) asserting that unsafe expressions in block content return `true`.
+- [ ] `BenchmarkCompileComplexWorkflow` shows no >10% regression relative to the baseline (as enforced by the CI benchstat gate in `cgo.yml`), and remains well below the `<500ms` baseline target documented in the test file.
+- [ ] No open issues reference a conformance failure against this ADR.
+
+Once all boxes are checked, update the `**Status**` field at the top of this document from `Draft` to `Accepted`.

+### Sync Task — Rename `GitHubAppConfig.AppID` to `GitHubAppConfig.ClientID`

github:github/gh-aw#48451.title: feat: add GitHub Copilot API endpoint as pricing data source in daily model inventory
github:github/gh-aw#48451.body:
The daily model inventory only fetched Copilot pricing via the internal reflect endpoint and a Playwright-scraped docs page. This adds `https://api.githubcopilot.com/models` as an additional candidate source, giving a direct API-based cross-check for `billing.multiplier` and surfacing models not yet visible through reflect.

## Changes

- **New pre-job `collect_copilot_api_models`**: fetches `https://api.githubcopilot.com/models` with a `copilot-requests: write` GitHub Actions token; normalizes each entry to `{id, name, vendor, capabilities, billing}` and uploads as `copilot-api-models` artifact. Graceful degradation on failure (error JSON written, source skipped by agent).
- **Permissions**: `copilot-requests: write` added to top-level workflow permissions and scoped to the new job only.
- **Agent prompt**: Step 3 adds the Copilot API as validation source #2 — supplementary `billing.multiplier` cross-check and new-model discovery alongside reflect (primary) and docs table (tertiary). Deprecated model exclusion rule and issue report template updated to cover the new source.

github:github/gh-aw#55214.title: Align daily workflow and merged-PR metrics
github:github/gh-aw#55214.body:
Daily reports used incompatible workflow populations and could compare Copilot merge outcomes against incomplete all-PR merge counts. This makes fleet-size and agent-attribution trends internally inconsistent.

- **Canonical workflow population**
  - Define `total_workflows` as direct `.github/workflows/*.md` sources.
  - Require source/lock basename parity before reporting counts.
  - Exclude nested shared components from fleet totals.

- **Comparable merge events**
  - Standardize daily merge comparisons on the previous complete UTC day.
  - Require paginated queries filtered by `window_start <= mergedAt < window_end`.
  - Treat incomplete retrieval as a lower bound, not an exact comparison value.

- **Copilot cohort semantics**
  - Separate merge events from PRs created in the reporting window.
  - Define `agent_prs_merged_from_created` as the creation-cohort success numerator.
  - Report success rate as N/A when no Copilot PRs were created.

```text
agent_prs_merged:              mergedAt within report window
agent_prs_merged_from_created: createdAt within report window and mergedAt != null
agent_success_rate:            merged_from_created / created
```

github:github/gh-aw#62415.title: Prevent Copilot CLI staging for Gemini ARC/DinD workflows
github:github/gh-aw#62415.body: Gemini workflows on ARC/DinD emitted a Copilot CLI staging step despite not installing Copilot. The generated `command -v copilot` failed before Gemini could start. - **Engine-aware staging** - Pass `stageCopilotCLI=false` from Gemini’s npm installation path. ```go return buildNpmEngineInstallStepsWithAWF(npmSteps, workflowData, false) ``` - **Regression coverage** - Compile an ARC/DinD Gemini workflow with firewall defaults. - Assert the generated lock file omits `Copy Copilot CLI to daemon-visible path`. - Fixes #61759 --- > Generated by [👨‍🍳 PR Sous Chef](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/actions/runs/35641565679) · pi · gpt54 · 41.9 AIC · ⊞ 9.1K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Agithub%2Fgh-aw+%22gh-aw-workflow-call-id%3A+github%2Fgh-aw%2Fpr-sous-chef%22&type=pullrequests) > Comment /souschef to run again

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,94 @@
+//go:build !integration
+
+package workflow
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"os"
+	"path/filepath"
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/github/gh-aw/pkg/stringutil"
+	"github.com/github/gh-aw/pkg/testutil"
+)
+
+func TestCompileWorkflow_ArcDindStagesCopilotCLIOnlyForCopilot(t *testing.T) {
+	const copilotStagingStepName = "Copy Copilot CLI to daemon-visible path"
+
+	for _, tc := range []struct {
+		engine    string
+		wantStage bool
+	}{
+		{engine: "claude"},
+		{engine: "gemini"},
+		{engine: "pi"},
+		{engine: "copilot", wantStage: true},
+	} {
+		t.Run(tc.engine, func(t *testing.T) {
+			workflow := fmt.Sprintf(`---
+on: workflow_dispatch
+engine: %s
+runner:
+  topology: arc-dind
+network:
+  allowed:
+    - defaults
+---
+
+# Test
+`, tc.engine)
+			testFile := filepath.Join(testutil.TempDir(t, tc.engine+"-arc-dind-test"), "test-workflow.md")
+			if err := os.WriteFile(testFile, []byte(workflow), 0644); err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+
+			if err := NewCompiler().CompileWorkflow(testFile); err != nil {
+				t.Fatalf("compile %s workflow: %v", tc.engine, err)
+			}
+
+			lockFile := stringutil.MarkdownToLockFile(testFile)
+			lockContent, err := os.ReadFile(lockFile)
+			if err != nil {
+				t.Fatalf("read lock file: %v", err)
+			}
+			if got := strings.Contains(string(lockContent), copilotStagingStepName); got != tc.wantStage {
+				t.Fatalf("Copilot CLI staging = %v, want %v", got, tc.wantStage)
+			}
+		})
+	}
+
+	t.Run("behavior-defined", func(t *testing.T) {
+		engine, err := NewBehaviorDefinedEngine(&EngineDefinition{
+			ID:          "custom",
+			DisplayName: "Custom",
+			Behaviors: &EngineBehaviorDefinition{
+				Installation: &EngineInstallationDefinition{
+					PackageManager:   "npm",
+					PackageName:      "custom",
+					Version:          "1.0.0",
+					StepName:         "Install Custom",
+					IncludeNodeSetup: true,
+				},
+				Execution: &EngineExecutionDefinition{
+					CommandName: "custom",
+					StepName:    "Execute Custom",
+				},
+			},
+		})
+		if err != nil {
+			t.Fatal(err)
+		}
+		steps := engine.GetInstallationSteps(&WorkflowData{
+			Name:         "test",
+			EngineConfig: &EngineConfig{ID: "custom"},
+			RunnerConfig: &RunnerConfig{Topology: RunnerTopologyArcDind},
+			NetworkPermissions: &NetworkPermissions{
+				Firewall: &FirewallConfig{Enabled: true},
+			},
+		})
+		if strings.Contains(strings.Join(flattenSteps(steps), "\n"), copilotStagingStepName) {
+			t.Fatal("behavior-defined workflow must not stage the Copilot CLI")
+		}
+	})
+}

github:github/gh-aw#47981.title: fix: remove duplicate warning icon in update output
github:github/gh-aw#47981.body:
`gh aw update` printed a double warning icon (`⚠ ⚠️`) when a locally modified workflow was detected. `console.FormatWarningMessage` already prepends `⚠ `, but the message string passed to it also contained a hardcoded `⚠️ ` prefix.

- **`pkg/cli/update_workflows.go`**: removed the redundant `⚠️ ` prefix from the format string

Before:
```
⚠ ⚠️  Local copy of ci-doctor has been modified from source
```

After:
```
⚠ Local copy of ci-doctor has been modified from source
```

files.patch:
@@ -671,7 +671,7 @@ func updateWorkflow(ctx context.Context, wf *workflowWithSource, opts UpdateWork
 		if hasLocalModifications(string(sourceContent), string(currentContent), wf.SourceSpec, filepath.Dir(wf.Path), opts.Verbose) {
 			updateLog.Printf("Local modifications detected in workflow: %s", wf.Name)
 			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, console.FormatInfoMessage(fmt.Sprintf("Workflow %s is already up to date (%s)", wf.Name, shortRef(currentRef))))
-			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, console.FormatWarningMessage(fmt.Sprintf("⚠️  Local copy of %s has been modified from source", wf.Name)))
+			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, console.FormatWarningMessage(fmt.Sprintf("Local copy of %s has been modified from source", wf.Name)))
 			return nil
 		}

github:github/gh-aw#56069.title: [eslint-miner] eslint-factory: add no-json-stringify-equality rule
github:github/gh-aw#56069.body:
`JSON.stringify()` output depends on object key insertion order, so comparing two stringify results with `===` reports deeply-equal values as unequal whenever the keys were inserted in a different order. This lands a lint rule for that pattern; the one live occurrence (`stateValuesEqual()` in `actions/setup/js/evaluate_outcomes.cjs`) is left for a follow-up.

**Flagged form:**
```js
return JSON.stringify(normalizedLeft) === JSON.stringify(normalizedRight);
```

### Changes

- **`src/rules/no-json-stringify-equality.ts`** (new) — reports `BinaryExpression` nodes with `===`/`!==`/`==`/`!=` where *both* operands are global `JSON.stringify(...)` calls. Reuses the scope-walk (`isGlobalReference`) from `no-json-stringify-set-or-map` so a locally shadowed `JSON` binding is ignored; the message interpolates the operator at the flagged site.
- **`src/rules/no-json-stringify-equality.test.ts`** (new) — covers all four operators, the real `stateValuesEqual` shape, and the valid cases below.
- **`src/index.ts`**, **`eslint.config.cjs`** (`"warn"`), **`README.md`** — registration, enablement, and docs, matching the neighboring rules and keeping the README/index parity test satisfied.

### Scoping (false-positive containment)

Requiring `JSON.stringify()` on *both* sides is what keeps this narrow — a single stringify compared against a literal or unrelated value has no key-order ambiguity. Not flagged:

- `JSON.stringify(value) === "{}"` (one operand)
- non-equality operators (`<`, `+`, …)
- `JSON.parse(...)`, non-`JSON` calls, shadowed `JSON`

Running `npm run lint:setup-js` surfaces exactly one occurrence, at `evaluate_outcomes.cjs:1057`.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

- Fixes #55995

+| [`no-json-stringify-equality`](#no-json-stringify-equality) | Disallow comparing two `JSON.stringify()` results for equality |

+### `no-json-stringify-equality`
+
+Disallow comparing two `JSON.stringify()` results with an equality operator (`===`, `!==`, `==`, `!=`). `JSON.stringify()` output depends on object key insertion order, so two deeply-equal objects built with keys inserted in a different order serialize to different strings and are reported as unequal.
+
+**Flagged form:**
+```js
+return JSON.stringify(normalizedLeft) === JSON.stringify(normalizedRight);
+```
+
+**Safe alternative:**
+```js
+return deepEqual(normalizedLeft, normalizedRight);
+```
+
+**Not flagged:**
+- `JSON.stringify(value) === "{}"` — only one operand is a `JSON.stringify()` call, so no key-order ambiguity exists.
+- Non-equality operators such as `<`, `>` or `+`.
+- A locally shadowed `JSON` binding.
+
 ### `no-json-stringify-set-or-map`
 
 Disallow `JSON.stringify()` directly on `Set` and `Map` instances. Their entries are not own enumerable properties, so serialization silently produces `{}`.

github:github/gh-aw#43302.title: fix: correct engine.env secrets warning — excluded from sandbox, not leaked
github:github/gh-aw#43302.body: The compiler incorrectly warned that secrets in `engine.env` *"will be leaked to the agent container"* even though `ComputeAWFExcludeEnvVarNames` already auto-detects `${{ secrets.` values in `engine.env` and adds them to AWF's `--exclude-env` list, keeping them out of the agent sandbox. ## Changes - **`pkg/workflow/strict_mode_env_validation.go`** — `validateEnvSecretsSection` now emits section-aware messages: - **`engine.env` non-strict warning**: replaced "will be leaked" with "will be excluded from the agent sandbox via awf `--exclude-env`; the agent process itself will not see these values directly" - **`engine.env` strict-mode error**: replaced "will be leaked" with "are auto-excluded from the agent sandbox via awf `--exclude-env` and are not accessible to the agent" — still an error (strict mode enforces engine-specific config), but no longer a false leakage claim - **Top-level `env`**: messages unchanged — secrets there genuinely reach the agent container - **`pkg/workflow/env_secrets_validation_test.go`** — updated three `engine.env` strict-mode test assertions to match the corrected error message text ### Before / After (non-strict, `engine.env`) ``` # Before ⚠ Warning: secrets detected in 'engine.env' section will be leaked to the agent container. Found: ${{ secrets.SOME_KEY }}. ... # After ⚠ Warning: secrets detected in 'engine.env' section will be excluded from the agent sandbox via awf --exclude-env; the agent process itself will not see these values directly. Found: ${{ secrets.SOME_KEY }}. ... ``` --- > Generated by [👨‍🍳 PR Sous Chef](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/actions/runs/28703187599) · 3.07 AIC · ⌖ 4.15 AIC · ⊞ 4.3K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Agithub%2Fgh-aw+%22gh-aw-workflow-call-id%3A+github%2Fgh-aw%2Fpr-sous-chef%22&type=pullrequests) > Comment /souschef to run again

@@ -0,0 +1,73 @@
+# ADR-43302: Section-Aware Secret Validation Messages in Workflow Compiler
+
+**Date**: 2026-07-04
+**Status**: Draft
+**Deciders**: Unknown
+
+---
+
+### Context
+
+The workflow compiler's `validateEnvSecretsSection` function validates secrets across multiple
+env sections (`env`, `engine.env`) and emits warnings or errors when `${{ secrets.* }}`
+references are detected. Historically it used a single generic message — "will be leaked to the
+agent container" — regardless of which section contained the secret reference.
+
+However, `engine.env` secrets are handled differently from top-level `env` secrets: the
+`ComputeAWFExcludeEnvVarNames` function auto-detects any `engine.env` value that contains a
+`${{ secrets.* }}` reference and adds the corresponding variable name to AWF's `--exclude-env`
+list. This means `engine.env` secrets never reach the agent sandbox process, making the
+"will be leaked" warning factually incorrect for that section and a source of user confusion.
+
+### Decision
+
+We will differentiate the validation messages emitted by `validateEnvSecretsSection` based on
+which section is being validated, rather than using a single generic message for all sections.
+For `engine.env`, messages will accurately reflect that secrets are auto-excluded from the
+agent sandbox via AWF `--exclude-env`; for all other sections (e.g., top-level `env`), the
+existing "will be leaked" language is retained because those secrets genuinely reach the
+agent container. Strict mode continues to treat `engine.env` secrets as an error (encouraging
+engine-specific secret configuration), but with accurate, non-misleading error text.
+
+### Alternatives Considered
+
+#### Alternative 1: Remove the `engine.env` warning entirely
+
+Since `engine.env` secrets are auto-excluded and never reach the agent process, one option is
+to suppress the warning entirely for that section — no message, no error. This eliminates the
+false positive and simplifies the code path. It was rejected because users should still be
+nudged toward engine-specific secret configuration (the more secure, explicit pattern), and
+removing all feedback would silently permit a configuration style that the platform discourages.
+
+#### Alternative 2: Extract a separate validation function for `engine.env`
+
+Rather than branching inside `validateEnvSecretsSection`, a dedicated
+`validateEngineEnvSecretsSection` function could own all `engine.env` secret logic. This would
+keep each function single-purpose and avoid section-name string comparisons. It was rejected
+for this fix because it would duplicate the secret-detection regex and collection logic that
+lives in `validateEnvSecretsSection`, increasing maintenance surface for a change whose primary
+goal is correcting a misleading string — not restructuring validation logic.
+
+### Consequences
+
+#### Positive
+- Users see accurate feedback: `engine.env` secret warnings now correctly describe sandbox
+  exclusion rather than falsely claiming leakage to the agent container.
+- Strict mode error messages for `engine.env` remain actionable and no longer contradict the
+  platform's actual security behavior, reducing support burden and user confusion.
+
+#### Negative
+- `validateEnvSecretsSection` now contains section-specific branching (`if sectionName == "engine.env"`),
+  slightly increasing cyclomatic complexity and making the function less generic.
+- Any future env section added to the validation path must be evaluated for whether it also
+  requires a custom message, creating an implicit maintenance contract.
+
+#### Neutral
+- Test assertions for `engine.env` strict-mode cases were updated to match the new message
+  text; this is a mechanical change with no behavioral impact on test coverage.
+- The `awf_helpers_test.go` additions verify the existing `ComputeAWFExcludeEnvVarNames`
+  behavior that this fix depends on for correctness, improving confidence in the invariant.
+
+---
+
+*ADR created by [adr-writer agent]. Review and finalize before changing status from Draft to Accepted.*

github:github/gh-aw#60349.title: Prevent Claude tool results from triggering failure classifiers
github:github/gh-aw#60349.body:
Claude stream-JSON includes tool results as `user` events, allowing benign repository content such as “not logged in” or `EACCES` to suppress retries or misreport failures.

- **Scope failure classification**
  - Exclude stream-JSON `user` events from auth, rate-limit, overload, permission-denied, and harness-guard classifiers.
  - Preserve result, system, assistant, malformed JSON, and plain-text output.
  - Continue using full output for session-progress and denied-command extraction.

- **Prioritize process termination**
  - Handle signal exits before authentication and permission-denied terminal rules.
  - Retry signal-terminated attempts as fresh runs with `--continue` disabled.

- **Cover regressions**
  - Verify tool-result text is excluded while result/plain-text errors remain classifiable.
  - Verify repeated permission errors in tool results are ignored.
  - Verify exit `143` retries even when classifiable authentication text is present.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

- Fixes #60282

github:github/gh-aw#43802.title: fix: address 7 CLI consistency issues from automated inspection
github:github/gh-aw#43802.body: Automated CLI consistency checker found 8 issues across help text and documentation. Addresses 7 of them (H1 is a false positive — `github.github.com` is the intentional configured docs host, validated by existing tests). ## Changes **M3 — `add-wizard` missing `--append` and `--no-security-scanner` flags** - Added both flags to `add-wizard`, matching their counterparts in `add` - Added `AppendText` and `DisableSecurityScanner` fields to `AddInteractiveConfig` - `add_interactive_git.go` now passes these through to `AddOptions` instead of hardcoding empty/false **M2 — `upgrade --pre-releases` example wording** - `"prerelease"` → `"pre-release"` (matches flag name spelling) - `"self-upgrading the extension"` → `"upgrading the extension"` (matches flag description wording) **M1 — `audit`/`logs` `--artifacts` default mismatch undocumented** - `logs`: `"default: usage — compact summary for faster downloads"` (also fixes L2 terminology gap) - `audit` + `audit-diff`: `"default: all, because auditing requires comprehensive artifacts for analysis"` **M4 — `env get`/`env update` `file.yml` placeholder ambiguity** - `"writes to file.yml"` → `"writes to file.yml in the current directory"` (literal, not a placeholder) **L1/L3 — Cosmetic** - `init --codespaces ""` example column alignment (off by one space vs aligned column) - Trailing whitespace after `# Create org project` in `project new` examples --- > Generated by [👨‍🍳 PR Sous Chef](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/actions/runs/28818440380) · 7.29 AIC · ⌖ 7.3 AIC · ⊞ 7.1K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Agithub%2Fgh-aw+%22gh-aw-workflow-call-id%3A+github%2Fgh-aw%2Fpr-sous-chef%22&type=pullrequests) > Comment /souschef to run again --- > Generated by [👨‍🍳 PR Sous Chef](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/actions/runs/28829827804) · 6.99 AIC · ⌖ 5.55 AIC · ⊞ 7.1K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Agithub%2Fgh-aw+%22gh-aw-workflow-call-id%3A+github%2Fgh-aw%2Fpr-sous-chef%22&type=pullrequests) > Comment /souschef to run again --- > Generated by [👨‍🍳 PR Sous Chef](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/actions/runs/28837945380) · 5.92 AIC · ⌖ 5.55 AIC · ⊞ 4.7K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Agithub%2Fgh-aw+%22gh-aw-workflow-call-id%3A+github%2Fgh-aw%2Fpr-sous-chef%22&type=pullrequests) > Comment /souschef to run again --- > Generated by [👨‍🍳 PR Sous Chef](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/actions/runs/28841046595) · 3.96 AIC · ⌖ 5.65 AIC · ⊞ 7.1K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Agithub%2Fgh-aw+%22gh-aw-workflow-call-id%3A+github%2Fgh-aw%2Fpr-sous-chef%22&type=pullrequests) > Comment /souschef to run again

github:github/gh-aw#45064.title: prefer-number-isnan: autofix provably numeric calls, keep cautionary suggestion for unknown inputs
github:github/gh-aw#45064.body: `prefer-number-isnan` treated all `isNaN(...)` calls as equally risky, so it always emitted a caveated suggestion even when the argument was already numeric. This change splits safe numeric cases from unknown-input cases so diagnostics and fix behavior match real semantics. - **Rule behavior: branch by argument certainty** - Added provably-numeric detection for single-argument calls: - `parseInt(...)`, `parseFloat(...)`, `Number(...)` - `Number.parseInt(...)`, `Number.parseFloat(...)` - numeric-returning method calls (`getTime`, `getTimezoneOffset`, `valueOf`) - numeric literals - When provably numeric: report with a direct message and provide **autofix** (`fix`) to `Number.isNaN(...)`. - When not provably numeric: preserve current **suggest-only** behavior and coercion caveat. - **Diagnostics/messages** - Split messages into: - non-caveated autofix path for provably numeric args - caveated suggest path for unknown/raw args - Retains the guard against silent semantic flips on string/unknown inputs. - **Tests** - Added autofix invalid cases for: - `isNaN(parseInt(value, 10))` - `isNaN(parseFloat(value))` - `isNaN(d.getTime())` - Kept unknown-input coverage (`isNaN(process.env.PORT)`) as suggest-only with caveat. - Updated existing expectations to use the new message IDs per branch. ```ts // autofix path (provably numeric) isNaN(parseInt(value, 10)); // => Number.isNaN(parseInt(value, 10)); // suggestion-only path (unknown/raw input) isNaN(process.env.PORT); // => suggest Number.isNaN(process.env.PORT) with Number(...) review caveat ``` --- > Generated by [👨‍🍳 PR Sous Chef](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/actions/runs/29202086164) · 6.24 AIC · ⌖ 5.58 AIC · ⊞ 7.5K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Agithub%2Fgh-aw+%22gh-aw-workflow-call-id%3A+github%2Fgh-aw%2Fpr-sous-chef%22&type=pullrequests) > Comment /souschef to run again --- > Generated by [👨‍🍳 PR Sous Chef](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/actions/runs/29202942828) · 10.1 AIC · ⌖ 6.32 AIC · ⊞ 7.5K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Agithub%2Fgh-aw+%22gh-aw-workflow-call-id%3A+github%2Fgh-aw%2Fpr-sous-chef%22&type=pullrequests) > Comment /souschef to run again

github:github/gh-aw#55574.title: Stabilize Daily Performance Summary 90-day metrics
github:github/gh-aw#55574.body:
The Daily Performance Summary could report large day-over-day swings because `updatedAt` was used as both the pagination boundary and the metric date. That made merged/resolved counts and backlog sensitive to unrelated updates inside the 90-day window.

- **Separate pagination from metric semantics**
  - Keep `updatedAt` as the query pagination boundary.
  - Filter total activity by `createdAt`.
  - Filter merged PR throughput by `mergedAt`.
  - Filter resolved issue throughput by `closedAt`.

- **Query backlog independently**
  - Fetch current open PRs and issues separately without the rolling `since` window.
  - Store them as `open_prs.json` and `open_issues.json` for backlog metrics.

- **Normalize timestamp handling**
  - Parse pandas timestamps with `utc=True` so comparisons use consistent timezone-aware values.

- **Add workflow contract coverage**
  - Added a focused test to lock the Daily Performance Summary prompt against regressing to `updatedAt`-based metric counting.

Example of the intended split:

```python
created_prs = pr_df[pr_df["createdAt"] >= ninety_days_ago]
merged_prs = pr_df[
    pr_df["mergedAt"].notna()
    & (pr_df["mergedAt"] >= ninety_days_ago)
]

created_issues = issue_df[issue_df["createdAt"] >= ninety_days_ago]
closed_issues = issue_df[
    issue_df["closedAt"].notna()
    & (issue_df["closedAt"] >= ninety_days_ago)
]
```

+package workflowcontract
+
+import (
+	"os"
+	"path/filepath"
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+)
+
+// TestDailyPerformanceSummaryUsesStableWindowMetrics verifies that the daily
+// performance prompt keeps updatedAt pagination separate from lifecycle metrics.
+// The tokens below are the stable contract surface; changing them requires
+// updating both the workflow source and this test.
+func TestDailyPerformanceSummaryUsesStableWindowMetrics(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+	content, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join("..", "..", ".github", "workflows", "daily-performance-summary.md"))
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("failed to read daily performance summary workflow source: %v", err)
+	}
+	text := string(content)
+
+	for _, token := range []string{
+		"window_start",
+		"createdAt >= window_start",
+		"mergedAt >= window_start",
+		"closedAt >= window_start",
+		"github-pr-query with state: \"all\", since: \"<window_start>\", jq: \".\"",
+		"github-pr-query with state: \"open\", limit: 1000, jq: \".\"",
+		"github-issue-query with state: \"all\", since: \"<window_start>\", jq: \".\"",
+		"github-issue-query with state: \"open\", limit: 1000, jq: \".\"",
+		"/tmp/gh-aw/python/data/open_prs.json",
+		"/tmp/gh-aw/python/data/open_issues.json",
+		"open_prs = load_json_data",
+		"open_issues = load_json_data",
+		"pd.to_datetime(pr_df['mergedAt'], utc=True)",
+		"pd.to_datetime(issue_df['closedAt'], utc=True)",
+		"pr_df['createdAt'] >= ninety_days_ago",
+		"(pr_df['mergedAt'] >= ninety_days_ago)",
+		"issue_df['createdAt'] >= ninety_days_ago",
+		"(issue_df['closedAt'] >= ninety_days_ago)",
+	} {
+		if !strings.Contains(text, token) {
+			t.Errorf("expected daily-performance-summary.md to contain token %q", token)
+		}
+	}
+}

github:github/gh-aw#53833.title: pr-sous-chef: document GraphQL fetch for reviewThreads (fixes invalid gh pr view field)
github:github/gh-aw#53833.body:
The `pr-processor` sub-agent prompt told the agent to read review-thread node IDs (`PRRT_...`) "from `reviewThreads`" without specifying a valid way to fetch it. In practice the agent guessed `gh pr view --json ...,reviewThreads,...`, which `gh` rejects (`Unknown JSON field: "reviewThreads"`), burning the sub-agent's tool-call budget on every scheduled run and falling through to skip/insufficient-context fallbacks instead of processing review threads.

- **Explicit data-fetch instructions**: added a note to the `pr-processor` prompt stating `gh pr view --json` has no `reviewThreads` field, with the correct `gh api graphql` query to fetch thread node IDs, resolution state, and comments.
- **Non-thread metadata**: documented the valid `gh pr view --json number,comments,reviews,headRefName,headRefOid,mergeStateStatus,title` call (without `reviewThreads`) for everything else.
- **Downstream clarity**: updated the "resolve review threads" step to point back at the GraphQL-sourced data and explicitly warn against `gh pr view --json reviewThreads`.
- **Lock file**: recompiled `pr-sous-chef.md` to regenerate `pr-sous-chef.lock.yml`.

```
gh api graphql -f query='query($owner:String!,$repo:String!,$pr:Int!){repository(owner:$owner,name:$repo){pullRequest(number:$pr){reviewThreads(first:100){nodes{id isResolved comments(first:10){nodes{author{login} body}}}}}}}' -f owner=github -f repo=gh-aw -F pr=<N>
```

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

- Fixes #53829

files.patch:
@@ -424,7 +424,7 @@ For each PR that is not skipped:
    - For `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch` runs, use the `resolve_review_threads` list returned by the `pr-processor` sub-agent.
    - Include a thread only when all of the following are true: the thread is currently unresolved; contains reviewer feedback; and has a later reply from the PR author or `@copilot`.
    - For each thread ID, call `safeoutputs resolve_pull_request_review_thread --thread_id <ID>`.
-   - Each `<ID>` must be the review thread node ID (`PRRT_...`) taken from `reviewThreads`; never pass a review comment node ID (`PRRC_...`).
+   - Each `<ID>` must be the review thread node ID (`PRRT_...`) taken from the `reviewThreads` data fetched via `gh api graphql` (see the `pr-processor` sub-agent instructions); never pass a review comment node ID (`PRRC_...`), and never fetch it via `gh pr view --json reviewThreads` (not a valid field).
    - Copy each `<ID>` verbatim, character-for-character, from the `reviewThreads` data returned for the current PR. Never guess, truncate, extend, or otherwise fabricate a thread ID.
    - If resolving one thread fails, record `{thread_id: <ID>, skip_reason: "resolve_review_thread_failed"}` in the `skipped` array and continue.
 
@@ -485,6 +485,10 @@ model: sonnet
 ---
 Given one PR number and compact metadata for `github/gh-aw`. Query only `github/gh-aw`; never use review thread or review IDs from another repository.
 
+- `gh pr view --json` has **no** `reviewThreads` field; requesting it fails with `Unknown JSON field: "reviewThreads"`. Never pass `reviewThreads` to `gh pr view --json`.
+- To fetch PR review thread node IDs (`PRRT_...`), issue this GraphQL query instead: `gh api graphql -f query='query($owner:String!,$repo:String!,$pr:Int!){repository(owner:$owner,name:$repo){pullRequest(number:$pr){reviewThreads(first:100){nodes{id isResolved comments(first:10){nodes{author{login} body}}}}}}}' -f owner=github -f repo=gh-aw -F pr=<N>` — the resulting `reviewThreads` array (from `data.repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads.nodes`) is the only valid source of `PRRT_...` IDs; each node's `id` is the thread ID and `isResolved` indicates resolution state.
+- Use `gh pr view <N> --repo github/gh-aw --json number,comments,reviews,headRefName,headRefOid,mergeStateStatus,title` (without `reviewThreads`) for all other PR metadata.
+
 1. Check skip conditions in this order:
    - checks/actions running — note: the candidate prefilter already excluded PRs with short-running pending checks (running < 1 hour) via `statusCheckRollup`; only re-verify if you have reason to believe state changed since the prefilter ran; Long-running checks (running > 1 hour) are intentionally ignored
    - latest comment contains both `<!-- gh-aw-pr-sous-chef-nudge -->` **and** `@copilot`, **and** `mergeStateStatus` is **not** `CONFLICTING` (when the branch has merge conflicts, do NOT skip even if the last actionable comment is from sous-chef — it must nudge Copilot to resolve them; also, comments with the marker but without `@copilot` are purely informational and do NOT count as a sous-chef nudge for this check)

github:github/gh-aw#43468.title: Fix allocation-size overflow risk in model pricing merge
github:github/gh-aw#43468.body:
CodeQL flagged `pkg/workflow/compiler_model_pricing.go` for allocation-size overflow in the workflow compiler’s model-pricing path. The issue was in capacity arithmetic used while cloning the top-level `ModelCosts` map.

- **Remove overflow-prone allocation math**
  - Stop pre-sizing the top-level clone in `mergeModelPricingIntoModelCosts`.
  - Let the map grow normally instead of deriving capacity from input size.

- **Add a regression guard**
  - Add a focused test that parses `compiler_model_pricing.go` and asserts the top-level `result` map allocation in `mergeModelPricingIntoModelCosts` does not reintroduce a capacity argument.

- **Preserve existing merge behavior**
  - Existing tests continue to cover merge correctness, non-mutation of input, and resolver behavior; this change narrows the security fix to allocation strategy only.

Example of the change:

```go
// before
result := make(map[string]any, len(modelCosts))

// after
result := make(map[string]any)
maps.Copy(result, modelCosts)
```

files.patch:
@@ -162,9 +162,9 @@ func mergeModelPricingIntoModelCosts(modelCosts map[string]any, provider, model
 	}
 	modelEntry := map[string]any{"cost": cost}
 
-	// Shallow-clone the top-level map. Do not add +1 here to avoid potential
-	// integer overflow; Go maps grow automatically as entries are added.
-	result := make(map[string]any, len(modelCosts))
+	// Shallow-clone the top-level map without pre-sizing to avoid reintroducing
+	// allocation-size arithmetic in this security-sensitive path.
+	result := make(map[string]any)
 	maps.Copy(result, modelCosts)
 
 	// Shallow-clone the providers map.

github:github/gh-aw#46551.title: fix: pin sub-agent models to claude-haiku-4.5 to resolve daily audit mismatches
github:github/gh-aw#46551.body:
Sub-agents declared with `model: small` were resolving to `claude-sonnet-4.6` at runtime. The Copilot engine doesn't resolve gh-aw model aliases — `small` passes through opaquely and the engine falls back to its default model.

## Workflow changes

Replace `model: small` with `model: claude-haiku-4.5` in the three flagged workflows:

- **`pr-description-caveman.md`** — `chunk-analyzer` sub-agent frontmatter
- **`code-simplifier.md`** — `scope-filter` and `simplification-scout` sub-agent frontmatter + body text references
- **`contribution-check.md`** — prompt instruction text for subagent dispatch calls

```diff
-model: small
+model: claude-haiku-4.5
```

## Contract tests

- Updated `contribution_check_workflow_contract_test.go` to assert `claude-haiku-4.5` instead of `small`
- Added `pr_description_caveman_workflow_contract_test.go` and `code_simplifier_workflow_contract_test.go` to enforce pinned Haiku model, matching the existing pattern in `pr-code-quality-reviewer.md`

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

- Fixes #46547

files.patch:
@@ -188,9 +188,9 @@ Code simplifier has nothing to process today.
 
 For each file in `source-files.json`:
 
-1. Use `scope-filter` (`model: small`) to confirm the file should be simplified and detect language.
+1. Use `scope-filter` (`model: claude-haiku-4.5`) to confirm the file should be simplified and detect language.
 2. Apply only the matching language skill guidance (do not load unrelated language guidance).
-3. Use `simplification-scout` (`model: small`) for extractive opportunity scoring.
+3. Use `simplification-scout` (`model: claude-haiku-4.5`) for extractive opportunity scoring.
 4. Make targeted edits that preserve behavior.
 
 Priorities:
@@ -260,7 +260,7 @@ Do not finish with plain text only. The safe-output tool call is required.
 ## agent: `scope-filter`
 ---
 description: Decides whether a candidate file should be simplified and labels its primary language
-model: small
+model: claude-haiku-4.5
 ---
 Input is a single file path string. Return strict JSON only:
 `{"path":"...","include":true|false,"language":"go|typescript|javascript|python|csharp|other","reason":"..."}`
@@ -270,7 +270,7 @@ Set `include` to false for tests, generated files, lockfiles, vendored code, or
 ## agent: `simplification-scout`
 ---
 description: Extractive scout that proposes low-risk simplification opportunities per file
-model: small
+model: claude-haiku-4.5
 ---
 Given file content, return strict JSON only:
 `{"path":"...","opportunities":[{"kind":"clarity|duplication|complexity|naming","summary":"...","risk":"low|medium"}]}`

@@ -158,7 +158,7 @@ Read the contents of `contributing-guidelines-truncated.md` from the workspace r
 
 Call the contribution-checker subagent for each PR with this prompt:
 
-Use `model: small` for every contribution-checker subagent call.
+Use `model: claude-haiku-4.5` for every contribution-checker subagent call.
 
 ```
 The CONTRIBUTING.md content for this repository is attached below (already truncated to 2000 chars by the pre-agent step).

@@ -141,7 +141,7 @@ If there are no meaningful changes, call `noop` instead.
 ## agent: `chunk-analyzer`
 ---
 description: Analyses one 400-line slice of a unified diff and extracts structured per-file change facts.
-model: small
+model: claude-haiku-4.5
 ---
 
 You receive a slice of a unified diff (`diff --git` format). Extract facts about every changed file found in this slice.

github:github/gh-aw#53413.title: Document why prefer-core-logging's stdout-safety exclusion doesn't extend to log/info/debug
github:github/gh-aw#53413.body:
The `prefer-core-logging` rule excludes `console.error`/`console.warn` from its `console.* → core.*` mapping to avoid corrupting stdio protocol channels, but applies no such exclusion to `console.log`/`console.info`/`console.debug`. The issue asked whether that asymmetry is a gap or intentional.

## Finding

Intentional. The corruption risk comes from the *stream change*, not from workflow commands:

| method | writes to | replacement | writes to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `console.error` / `console.warn` | **stderr** | `core.error` / `core.warning` | **stdout** (workflow command) |
| `console.log` / `console.info` | stdout | `core.info` | stdout (plain message) |
| `console.debug` (alias of `console.log`) | stdout | `core.debug` | stdout (`::debug::` command) |

For log/info/debug both sides use stdout, so the substitution cannot dirty a previously clean protocol channel — a process that owns stdout for framing is already corrupting it by calling `console.log` at all. Only the error/warn case migrates stderr traffic onto stdout.

Verified against `@actions/core`: `info()` is `process.stdout.write(message + os.EOL)`; `debug()`, `error()`, `warning()`, and `notice()` all go through `issueCommand`, which also writes to stdout.

## Changes

- **`src/rules/prefer-core-logging.ts`** — extended the `CONSOLE_TO_CORE` comment with the confirmed stream behavior for both sides, and an explicit note that the asymmetry must not be collapsed in a future refactor.
- **`README.md`** — added a "Why the exclusion does not extend to `log` / `info` / `debug`" subsection under the existing exclusion docs.
- **`src/rules/prefer-core-logging.test.ts`** — two cases pinning the behavior for stdio-protocol-owning file contexts:

```ts
{
  filename: "actions/setup/js/mcp_server_core.cjs",
  code: `console.log("server starting");`,
  errors: [{ messageId: "preferCoreLogging", data: { method: "log", replacement: "core.info" }, /* ... */ }],
}
```

No rule logic changed.

- Fixes #53311

github:github/gh-aw#44286.title: fix: default sink-visibility to "public" when repository visibility check fails
github:github/gh-aw#44286.body:
When the `determine-automatic-lockdown` step fails to fetch repository visibility, `sink-visibility` was set to `"unknown"` — an unrecognised value that guard policy enforcement could handle unpredictably.

## Changes

- **`determine_automatic_lockdown.cjs`**: Change `visibility` fallback in the `catch` block from `"unknown"` → `"public"`, and update the warning message to name the default explicitly.
- **`determine_automatic_lockdown.test.cjs`**: Update the API-failure test assertion to expect `"public"`.

## Rationale

`"public"` is the safe conservative choice: it forces `min-integrity='approved'` + `repos='all'`, i.e. the same strict policy applied to public repos. Defaulting to an unknown string risks the guard treating it as unrecognised and applying no policy.

github:github/gh-aw#47380.title: Add regression coverage for PR review path-resolution fallback
github:github/gh-aw#47380.body:
GitHub can reject inline PR review comments with 422 `"Path could not be resolved"` in the same fallback family as `"Line could not be resolved"`. This path-based variant was not covered by tests, leaving the safe-output body/partial-anchor fallback effectively unvalidated.

- **What changed**
  - Added a focused regression test in `actions/setup/js/pr_review_buffer.test.cjs` for a review submission that fails with:
    - `message: "Path could not be resolved"`
    - `field: "comments[1].path"`
  - The test verifies the existing fallback behavior:
    - resolvable comments are retried inline
    - the unresolvable comment is appended to the review body
    - the retry warning remains informative

- **Why this matters**
  - Covers the path-based 422 variant in the same reviewer fallback path as line-resolution failures
  - Reduces the chance of this class of API validation errors turning reviewer runs red without preserving review content

- **Example scenario covered**
  ```js
  const unresolvedError = new Error('Unprocessable Entity: "Path could not be resolved"');
  unresolvedError.response = {
    data: {
      errors: [{ field: "comments[1].path", message: "Path could not be resolved" }],
    },
  };
  ```

github:github/gh-aw#46190.title: Refine require-new-url-try-catch safe-argument detection
github:github/gh-aw#46190.body:
`require-new-url-try-catch` was over-classifying some `new URL(...)` calls as runtime-risky. In particular, it flagged provably constant string concatenations and `new URL(import.meta.url)`, even though both are syntactically safe and non-throwing in the cases covered here.

- **Rule precision**
  - teach the rule to treat recursively constant string expressions as static:
    - string literals
    - expression-less template literals
    - `+` concatenations composed only of the above
  - reuse the existing `import.meta.url` safe-value exemption for the first argument, not just the base argument

- **Behavioral effect**
  - stop reporting false positives such as:
    ```js
    new URL("https://github.com" + "/owner/repo");
    const u = new URL(import.meta.url);
    ```
  - keep reporting genuinely dynamic inputs, including variable-based concatenation:
    ```js
    const u = new URL(host + "/x");
    ```

- **Coverage**
  - add valid-case tests for constant concatenation and `import.meta.url` in first-argument position
  - add an invalid regression test confirming variable concatenation remains in scope

github:github/gh-aw#58625.title: Preserve setup-action PATH across privileged AWF startup
github:github/gh-aw#58625.body:
`docker-sudo-iptables` allowed sudo’s `secure_path` to replace the runner PATH before AWF captured it, causing setup-selected runtimes such as Ruby 3.4.8 to resolve to system versions instead.

### Changes

- **Privileged invocation**
  - Restore the caller’s PATH after sudo.
  - Execute AWF through trusted absolute paths to prevent PATH-based binary substitution.

```bash
sudo -E /usr/bin/env PATH="$PATH" /usr/local/bin/awf
```

- **Regression coverage**
  - Model the sudo boundary with selected, system, and cached Ruby versions.
  - Verify the setup-selected Ruby retains precedence while cache-only tools remain discoverable.

- **Generated workflow**
  - Refresh the `docker-sudo-iptables` service-port smoke workflow lock file.

+	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(secureBin, "ruby"), []byte("#!/bin/sh\necho 'ruby 3.2.3'\n"), 0o755))

+	awfScript := fmt.Sprintf("#!/bin/bash\nset -e\nunset GOROOT ERLANG_HOME\n%s\nruby --version\nnpm-agent\n", GetNpmBinPathSetup())
+	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(fakeAWF, []byte(awfScript), 0o755))

+if [ "$1" = "-E" ]; then

+

+		},
+	}

+	hostPath := strings.Join([]string{selectedRubyBin, commandBin, "/usr/bin", "/bin"}, ":")
+	securePath := strings.Join([]string{secureBin, "/usr/bin", "/bin"}, ":")
+	shellCmd := fmt.Sprintf(
+		`export PATH=%q GH_AW_TEST_SECURE_PATH=%q RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE=%q; %s`,
+		hostPath,
+		securePath,
+		cacheRoot,
+		awfCommand,
+	)

github:github/gh-aw#55529.title: Fix conclusion job issues permission derivation
github:github/gh-aw#55529.body:
Threat detection could re-add `issues: write` to the generated `conclusion` job even when all configured issue-creating safe outputs were disabled. This regressed reusable workflows with restricted permission ceilings.

- **Permission derivation**
  - Stop treating an enabled detection job as sufficient to grant `issues: write`.
  - Derive the grant from configured conclusion issue-creation paths only.
  - Restore `missing-tool.create-issue` as an explicit contributor to the grant.

- **Regression coverage**
  - Cover the reported shape: default threat detection enabled, issue-creating outputs disabled, `update-release` still requiring `contents: write`.

```yaml
conclusion:
  permissions:
    contents: write
```

github:github/gh-aw#53424.title: Triage aging CodeQL alert #564: prefer gh extension install over curl|bash in README
github:github/gh-aw#53424.body:
CodeQL alert #564 (`workflow-security-finding-1`) flagged the `curl | bash` install pattern in README.md's agent-bootstrap instructions as the oldest of the repo's open alerts, with no dedicated tracking issue.

## README install instructions

- Reordered the "Configure this project with agentic workflows" section to lead with `gh extension install github/gh-aw` as the primary install method, avoiding an unreviewed remote script piped directly into a shell.
- Kept the standalone `curl | bash` installer as a documented fallback for when `gh` isn't available, noting it performs SHA256 checksum verification by default.
- Mirrors the install guidance structure already used in `docs/src/content/docs/setup/cli.md`.

```bash
# primary
gh extension install github/gh-aw

# fallback if gh isn't available (checksum-verified by default)
curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/gh-aw/main/install-gh-aw.sh | bash
```

## Incidental fix

- Restored `pkg/workflow/schemas/github-workflow.json`, which had been overwritten with a GitHub `429: Too Many Requests` response body by an unrelated rate-limited fetch during an earlier automated commit step. Content and validity confirmed against the prior good version.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

- Fixes #53418

github:github/gh-aw#49314.title: fix(gh-aw-node): patch bundled tar/brace-expansion CVEs, bump npm to 11.19.0
github:github/gh-aw#49314.body:
The `gh-aw-node` image (`ghcr.io/github/gh-aw-node`) had 6 grype-reported vulnerabilities: Alpine base CVEs (CVE-2026-58055, CVE-2025-60876) and vulnerable npm-bundled packages (`tar@7.5.19`, `brace-expansion@5.0.7`).

## Changes

- **`Dockerfile.safe-outputs-mcp`**
  - Bump `NPM_VERSION` `11.18.0` → `11.19.0`
  - After the global npm install, explicitly upgrade npm's own bundled `tar` and `brace-expansion` to patched versions:
    ```dockerfile
    && npm install --prefix "$(npm root -g)/npm" --no-save "tar@^7.5.22" "brace-expansion@^5.0.8" \
    ```
    Neither npm 11.x nor 12.x currently bundles these at the required minimums (`tar≥7.5.21`, `brace-expansion≥5.0.8`), so the explicit override is necessary.
  - Alpine CVEs are already covered by the existing `apk upgrade --no-cache` on each rebuild.

- **`.changeset/patch-refresh-gh-aw-node.md`** — updated to document the CVEs and remediation.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

- Fixes #49295

files.patch:
@@ -2,4 +2,4 @@
 "gh-aw": patch
 ---
 
-Refresh the `gh-aw-node` image's Alpine and npm packages and publish it for both amd64 and arm64.
+Refresh the `gh-aw-node` image's Alpine and npm packages and publish it for both amd64 and arm64. Bump npm to 11.19.0 and patch bundled `tar` to ≥7.5.22 and `brace-expansion` to ≥5.0.8 to address container security findings (CVE-2026-58055, CVE-2025-60876, and related npm dependency vulnerabilities).

@@ -7,13 +7,16 @@ ARG NODE_IMAGE
 ARG NODE_IMAGE_DIGEST=""
 ARG NODE_IMAGE_UPDATED_AT=""
 ARG DOCKERFILE_HASH=""
-ARG NPM_VERSION=11.18.0
+ARG NPM_VERSION=11.19.0
 
 # Intentional: upgrade all packages to pick up security fixes; downstream digest pins the result.
+# After upgrading npm, patch its bundled dependencies to meet minimum safe versions
+# (tar >= 7.5.21 for CVE-2025-tar, brace-expansion >= 5.0.8 for CVE-2025-brace-expansion).
 RUN apk upgrade --no-cache \
     && apk add --no-cache git \
     && apk info -v | sort \
     && npm install --global "npm@${NPM_VERSION}" \
+    && npm install --prefix "$(npm root -g)/npm" --no-save "tar@^7.5.22" "brace-expansion@^5.0.8" \
     && npm cache clean --force
 
 LABEL org.opencontainers.image.source="https://github.com/github/gh-aw" \
